```{python}
import polars as pl
import requests #new for reading in JSON
import io       #new for reading in JSON
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```



```{python}
# Learn morea about Code Cells: https://quarto.org/docs/reference/cells/cells-jupyter.html

url = "https://byuidatascience.github.io/DS250-Course-Polars/Data/house-price.json"
response = requests.get(url)
df = pl.read_json(io.BytesIO(response.content))
```



Lesson Objectives

- Understand JSON
- Work with conditional logic
- Review expression expansion (regex and case selectors)
- explore some other geoms for graphing



## Conditional Logic

```{python}
df_adj = (
    df.with_columns(
        price_adj = 
            pl.when(pl.col("furnishingstatus") == "unfurnished")
              .then(pl.col("price") + 5000 * pl.col("area") / 1000)
              .when(pl.col("furnishingstatus") == "semi-furnished")
              .then(pl.col("price") + 2000 * pl.col("area") / 1000)
              .otherwise(pl.col("price"))
    )
)

```



## Review expression expansion


Let's divide price and price_adj by 1000.

```{python}
(
    df_adj.with_columns((pl.col(["price", "price_adj"]) / 1000).name.suffix("_k"))
)

```


Regular expression

```{python}
df_adj.with_columns((pl.col("^\w*price\w*$") / 1000).name.suffix("_k"))
```



Column selectors


```{python}
import polars.selectors as cs

df_adj.select(cs.contains("price"))
df_adj.select(cs.numeric())

# Select columns by data type.
df_adj.select(pl.col(pl.Int64))
df_adj.select(pl.col(pl.Float64))
df_adj.select(pl.col([pl.Int64, pl.Float64])) # all numeric
df_adj.select(pl.col(pl.String))
```


## Convert between datatype


```{python}
(
    df_adj.with_columns(pl.col("bedrooms").cast(pl.String))
          .with_columns(pl.col("bedrooms").cast(pl.Int64))
)

```




```{python}
(
    ggplot(data=df_adj, mapping=aes(x="bedrooms", y="area"))
    + geom_violin()
    +geom_jitter(color = "blue", alpha = .05)
)
```




```{python}
(
    ggplot(data=df_adj, mapping=aes(x="area"))
    + geom_density()
    + facet_wrap(facets="bedrooms")
)
```




# Unit 2 Day 2


Lesson outcome

- simple column aggregation, vertical summary statistic.
- group_by() aggregation



## Basic aggregation


```{python}
mykids = [22, 20, 17, 14, 12]
sum(mykids)
```





```{python}
df.select(pl.col("price").median())
# to get the # without the dataframe structure
df.select(pl.col("price").median().item())
```


multiple calculations in one step


```{python}
df.select(
    pl.col("price").median().alias("med_price"),
    pl.col("price").max().alias("max_price"),
    (pl.col(["area", "bedrooms"]).mean()).name.suffix("_mean")
)
```



Ne need to recreate the wheel




```{python}
df.describe()
```



# group_by().agg()


```{python}
df.group_by("bedrooms").agg(
    pl.mean("area", "stories"), 
    pl.max("price").alias("max_price"),
    pl.len()
)
```



Repeat the calculation but with different syntax
```{python}
df.group_by("bedrooms").agg(
    pl.col(["area", "stories"]).mean(),
    pl.col("price").max().alias("max_price"),
    pl.len()
)
```



## Lest columns and conditional calculations




```{python}
(
    df.group_by("bedrooms")
      .agg(
        pl.col("guestroom").alias("popcorn"),
        (pl.col("guestroom") == "yes").sum(),
        (pl.col("guestroom") == "yes").mean().alias("prop"),
    )
)
```




## nested group_by




```{python}
(
    df.group_by("bedrooms", "bathrooms")
      .agg(
        pl.col("price").median(),
        pl.len()
      )
)

```


# over()

```{python}
(
    df.with_columns(
        pl.col("price").median().over("bedrooms", "bathrooms").alias("med_price")`
    )
)
```
